rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT method (plane-wave pseudopotential, PBE functional) applied to a well-known crystal prototype; formation energies, elastic constants via strain, and Debye temperature are calculated using routine formulas. The task requires no novel algorithm or deep math just careful setup of substitution sites and convergence criteria.
rationale.execution: The workflow requires ~4-6 stages: structure generation, elemental reference calculations, geometry optimizations for multiple candidate structures (selecting the most stable), elastic constant calculations, and post-processing to derive elastic moduli, Debye temperature, and thermal conductivity. Several DFT runs must be managed, but the orchestration is sequential and uses a single open-source code.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT (PBE) to compute formation energies, elastic constants, and derived thermodynamic properties for a series of doped intermetallics. The method is routine in computational materials science; no novel algorithms or deep theoretical derivations are required. The pipeline involves multiple DFT runs and post-processing steps, but using a commonly available code (Quantum ESPRESSO) with moderate orchestration. Resources are CPU-only for small cell calculations.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT on small unit cells (20 atoms) using a plane-wave code (Quantum ESPRESSO) with moderate k-point sampling; CPU-only with typical memory footprint of a few GB; no large dataset required.
